name: Florida's B.E.S.T. Standards for Mathematics
checked: 2026-10-01: every K–5 benchmark read from FDOE's grade-level B.E.S.T. mathematics files (Kindergarten to Grade 5)
note: Summaries are our own one-line wording; the official text stays at the source. source_url is the Kindergarten file; rows for Grades 1 to 5 carry their own grade file. Codes are the full benchmark codes (MA.3.NSO.2.4); the form without MA. (3.NSO.2.4) is an alias. The standard (MA.3.NSO.2) is the cluster, not a row. The K–12 Mathematical Thinking and Reasoning standards (MA.K12.MTR) are not grade codes and are left out, like Common Core's practice standards.

standards.summary: Count up to 20 objects, write how many, and know the count stays the same when the objects are moved.
Count out a set of objects for a number from 0 to 20.
Name positions in a line from first to fifth.
Compare two groups of up to 20 objects as less than, equal to or greater than.
Say the numbers to 100 by ones and tens, count on within 100 from any number, and count back within 20.
Show numbers from 10 to 20 as a ten and some ones with objects, drawings or equations.
Place, order and compare numbers from 0 to 20 on a number line.
Explore adding two numbers from 0 to 10, and the related subtraction, with objects, drawings, number lines and equations.
Add two one-digit numbers with sums to 10, and subtract with the related facts, reliably.
Find the number that goes with 1 to 9 to make 10.
Show numbers from 0 to 10 as sums of two numbers in different ways.
Solve add and subtract story problems within 10 with objects, drawings or equations.
Explain why an addition or subtraction equation is true, using objects or drawings.
standards.scope_note: Explanations can only be checked as choices.

standards.summary: Name things about an object that can be measured, such as length, volume or weight.
standards.scope_note: Describing in words is limited to choosing attribute names.

standards.summary: Compare two objects directly and describe the difference with words like longer or heavier.
Give a length up to 20 units by laying same-size objects end to end.
standards.scope_note: Shown with on-screen units, not real objects.

standards.summary: Name circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders, whatever their size or position.

standards.summary: Sort objects into categories, count each one, and compare the categories.
standards.scope_note: Gathering is hands-on; sorting and showing given data is on screen.
